name: Uniform Inversion, Positive Binary Quadratic Forms and Hermitian Kernels
description: Proves compact-uniform reciprocal convergence, critical-circle modulus from positivity, and positive-semidefinite Gram realizations for based Hermitian kernels.

program.name: Statistical and Analytic Instances
program.summary: The statistics results build finite stochastic channels and parametric families, prove Fisher data processing under a fixed Markov kernel and the finite Cramér-Rao bound, and give the sharp quadratic bound on binary entropy. The analytic results give positivity of integer binary quadratic forms, uniform inversion under compact separation and Hermitian kernel realizations.

oneLine: On an open set, a family compact-uniformly separated from zero and converging locally uniformly has reciprocals converging locally uniformly; nonnegativity of x^2 + a*x*y + q*y^2 at all integer vectors is equivalent to a^2 <= 4*q and gives every zero of X^2 - a*X + q modulus sqrt q; and every finite Gram matrix of a based Hermitian kernel is positive semidefinite and realized by Euclidean feature vectors.
summary: The theory studies sequences of complex functions, the real binary form x^2 + a*x*y + q*y^2 with its complex quadratic X^2 - a*X + q, and based Hermitian kernels with Gram matrices and Euclidean feature vectors. Its questions are the conditions for inversion to preserve locally uniform convergence, for positivity of the form to force a discriminant bound and a root modulus, and for finite kernel samples to admit positive-semidefinite Gram realizations. For inversion, on an open set U, compact-uniform separation from zero plus locally uniform convergence yields locally uniform convergence of the reciprocals, a uniform version holds on a set K under an eventual positive lower bound, and the family 1/(n+1), nonzero at every point, fails compact-uniform separation on the whole plane. For positivity, nonnegativity of the form at all integer vectors is equivalent to nonnegativity at all real vectors and to a^2 <= 4*q, by rational scaling and continuity, and it gives positive semidefiniteness of the matrix with rows [1, a/2] and [a/2, q] and modulus sqrt q for every zero of X^2 - a*X + q. For kernels, every finite-sample Gram matrix is Hermitian and positive semidefinite and is realized by Euclidean feature vectors, any realizing vectors have squared distances given by kernel values, and a two-point kernel on Fin 2 takes the value 1 at (1, 1). The explicit roots have modulus sqrt q under 0 <= q and a^2 <= 4*q, the factorization through them needs only a^2 <= 4*q, the real-vector discriminant theorem carries the premise 0 < q, the general transport from integer to real vectors needs a finite index type, continuity and degree-two homogeneity, one discriminant version takes a citation-carrier premise, and the critical-circle file states that it claims no consequence for the Riemann hypothesis.
boundary: On an open set, compact-uniform separation from zero is a sufficient condition for pointwise inversion to preserve locally uniform convergence; the reciprocal theorems prove sufficiency only. The family 1/(n+1) is nonzero at every point and fails compact-uniform separation on the whole plane, so pointwise nonvanishing does not give the separation hypothesis. For the quadratic form, nonnegativity at all real vectors, equivalently at all integer vectors, holds exactly when a^2 <= 4*q, and on that side the factorization through the explicit roots and the root-modulus theorems place every zero of X^2 - a*X + q on the circle of radius sqrt q.

conclusions.statement: If U is open in ℂ, F is compact-uniformly separated from zero on U, and F converges locally uniformly on U to f, then the reciprocal family fun n z => (F n z)⁻¹ converges locally uniformly on U to fun z => (f z)⁻¹.
If there exist ε > 0 and N with ε ≤ ‖F n z‖ for all n ≥ N and z ∈ K, and F converges uniformly on K to f, then fun n z => (F n z)⁻¹ converges uniformly on K to fun z => (f z)⁻¹.
If integerLatticePositivity a q holds and quadraticValue a q z = 0, then the norm of z equals sqrt q.
If 0 < q and commitQuadratic a q x y >= 0 for all real x and y, then a^2 <= 4*q.
If integerLatticePositivity a q holds, with no citation premise, then a^2 <= 4*q.
If 0 <= q and a^2 <= 4*q and quadraticValue a q z = 0, then the norm of z equals sqrt q.
If 0 <= q and a^2 <= 4*q, then the norm of criticalRootPlus a q equals sqrt q and the norm of criticalRootMinus a q equals sqrt q.
If a^2 <= 4*q, then for every complex z, quadraticValue a q z equals (z - criticalRootPlus a q)*(z - criticalRootMinus a q).
integerLatticePositivity a q holds if and only if commitQuadratic a q x y >= 0 for all real x and y, and holds if and only if a^2 <= 4*q.

If integerLatticePositivity a q holds, then commitQuadratic a q x y is nonnegative for all real x and y; more generally, if the index type has Fintype and f from real vectors to reals is continuous and homogeneous of degree two with f (t • x) = t^2 * f x and is nonnegative at every integer vector, then for the given real vector x, 0 <= f x.
If integerLatticePositivity a q holds, then commitMatrix a q is positive semidefinite.

For any based Hermitian kernel H and any finite sample x indexed by Fin n, the Gram matrix kernelGram H.K x is Hermitian and positive semidefinite and there exist vectors v i in EuclideanSpace over Fin n with inner (v i) (v j) = H.K (x i) (x j) for all i j.

For any based Hermitian kernel H, any finite sample x, and any vectors v satisfying inner (v i) (v j) = H.K (x i) (x j) for all i j, the squared distance satisfies norm (v i - v j)^2 = (H.K (x i) (x i)).re + (H.K (x j) (x j)).re - 2*(H.K (x i) (x j)).re for all i j.
There is a based Hermitian kernel on Fin 2 with base 0 whose kernel is the inner product of the fixture sending 0 to 0 and other points to the constantly 1 vector, and its value at (1, 1) equals 1.
It is false that guardExpiryFamily is compact-uniformly separated from zero on univ.

openPoints: Locally uniform reciprocal convergence needs the set to be open, plus compact-uniform separation and locally uniform convergence; the compact version needs an eventual uniform positive lower bound and uniform convergence on that compact set.
Real discriminant bound carries a 0 < q hypothesis; explicit root and general zero modulus statements carry 0 <= q with a^2 <= 4*q; factorization needs only a^2 <= 4*q.
One integer discriminant version carries a citation-carrier premise in addition to 0 < q and lattice positivity, while the direct version needs only lattice positivity.
Generic homogeneous transport needs a Fintype index, continuity, degree-two homogeneity, and nonnegativity at integer vectors.
The file reports no consequence for the Riemann hypothesis.
Gram and realization results hold for every finite sample; the distance identity additionally requires feature vectors reproducing the kernel values.

files.summary: The file defines compact-uniform separation from zero for a sequence of complex functions, requiring an eventual uniform positive lower bound on each compact subset. It proves that such separation together with uniform convergence on a compact set yields uniform convergence of the pointwise reciprocals, and hence that separation plus locally uniform convergence on an open set yields locally uniform convergence of reciprocals. It also defines the constant-in-space family F n z = 1/(n+1) and proves it is not compact-uniformly separated on univ, although each stage is pointwise nonzero.
files.conclusion: On an open set in ℂ, compact-uniform separation from zero together with locally uniform convergence implies locally uniform convergence of the pointwise reciprocals.

files.summary: The file defines the real binary form commitQuadratic and its integer-lattice nonnegativity, the complex polynomial quadraticValue with its two explicit roots criticalRootPlus and criticalRootMinus, and the symmetric matrix commitMatrix. It proves that real positivity forces the discriminant inequality a^2 <= 4*q, and that under this inequality the polynomial factors and every zero has modulus sqrt q. It transports integer positivity to rationals by clearing denominators and to reals by continuity and density, giving equivalences with real positivity and with the discriminant, plus a generic homogeneous degree-two transport lemma and matrix positive-semidefiniteness. It claims no consequence for the Riemann hypothesis.
files.conclusion: Integer-lattice nonnegativity of x^2 + a*x*y + q*y^2 is equivalent to a^2 <= 4*q and forces every complex zero of X^2 - a*X + q to have modulus sqrt q.

files.summary: This file defines based Hermitian kernels: complex kernels with a distinguished base point where the kernel vanishes, Hermitian symmetry, and positive-semidefinite finite quadratic forms, together with their Gram matrices and quadratic forms. It proves that every finite-sample Gram matrix is Hermitian and positive semidefinite. It then proves a finite Kolmogorov realization giving Euclidean feature vectors whose inner products reproduce the kernel values, packaged with the PSD claim. It also proves the feature-distance identity expressing squared feature distance through kernel values, and constructs a nonzero two-point example on Fin 2 with value 1 at (1, 1).
files.conclusion: Every finite sample of a based Hermitian kernel has a positive semidefinite Gram matrix realized by Euclidean feature vectors whose squared distances are given by kernel values.

relationsIn.statement: The metric diagonal grade D1u is proved equivalent to compact-uniform separation from zero, and the reciprocal convergence theorem for that separation transfers to D1u.
